name: Painter stage
responsibility: Holds one canvas's picture, how it is seen and everything that moves on it, takes the page's decisions whole, and draws a frame at a moment of its own clock
description: Seven names (ADR 0085): Stage::new(theme, size, Pace), present(Presentation), arrive(Painting, Arrival), depart(Departure), draw(Surface, now) -> Motion and pick. The pace, a move's phases and the longest step of the clock, comes at birth. A presentation states only what changed: each value it states replaces the last, and a value it leaves out stays. An arrival is a cut, a carry, an entrance or a flight into a card; a departure is a leaving, a stay, a clear or the end of a flight into a card, so the page states each decision once and in no required order within a turn. The stage owns its clock. Each timed value carries its own moment (the camera, the awaited step, the light, a sweep, an entrance, a flight into a card and a leaving), and the stage reads the clock once for each such moment and once for each frame, so a stepped clock records it frame by frame. A cut, a carry, a stay, a clear and a sweep with no lines name no moment and read nothing. Each draw says whether to keep a strip canvas's parts: Surface::Strips wraps the canvas in the stage's part store and culls to the stage's size, and Surface::Direct draws whole, as the GPU canvas, a recording canvas and a counting canvas need. A frame answers its Motion: still, traffic alone or moving.
